in_text_mentions: Stage III vulvar carcinoma is defined as inguinal node involvement (Figure 5). When it affects one or two inguinal lymph nodes < 5 mm or a single inguinal lymph node ≥ 5 mm, it is classified as stage IIIA. Stage IIIB is defined as involvement of two or more inguinal lymph nodes ≥ 5 mm or three or more < 5 mm. Stage IIIC is defined as positive lymph nodes with extracapsular spread.

Only three metastatic deposits within the inguinal lymph nodes showed positive staining for vimentin. Local tumor recurrence. Note the higher degree of tumor differentiation with abundance of keratinous pearls in this representative histological field (hematoxylin and eosin stain). Bars are 100 μm in A, B, D, F; 50 μm in E and D inset; 25 μm C.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Gross clinical photograph of the vulva showing bleeding, vegetative (exophytic fungating) lesions; the caption ('vulvar bleeding vegetants lesions') and the article title (early invasive vulvar squamous cell carcinoma) directly support attribution to vulvar SCC. [raw subtype: early_invasive] b: Low-power H&E histology of the vulvar biopsy showing a micropapillary growth pattern; per the caption and article this represents the invasive vulvar SCC arising in a background of pemphigus vulgaris. [raw subtype: early_invasive] c: High-power H&E showing atypical mitotic figures supporting invasive vulvar SCC, with coexisting acantholytic clefts from the background pemphigus vulgaris; the in-text explicitly notes 'dysplastic cells with atypical mitoses' in this figure. [raw subtype: early_invasive]

Most recently, at gynaecological examination a thick area associated with ulcerative necrotic areas, and atypical vessels were revealed. Vulvar biopsy diagnosed PV. The epidermidis was arranged in a micropapillary pattern with combined aspects of acantholytic and atypical cells. Multiple areas of acantholytic clefts separated the upper part of the epidermidis from the basal keratinocytes. Unusually, dysplastic cells with atypical mitoses were present (Figure 1). Because she was virgin , She never had a pap smear and we did not perform it.
